title: Bengaluru Weather Explorer
tagline: Pull daily NASA POWER weather from a live API, chart the monsoon, and set a next-day forecast baseline.
question: What does a decade of Bengaluru weather look like, and how hard is tomorrow's temperature to predict?
audience: Beginners who want to work with a real scientific API instead of a static CSV.

source.name: NASA POWER Daily API
source.publisher: NASA Langley Research Center - POWER Project
source.license: NASA open data - no restrictions; acknowledgement requested
source.citation: Data obtained from the NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER Project funded through the NASA Earth Science/Applied Science Program.

lesson.title: -999 is not a temperature
lesson.summary: POWER marks missing values with a fill value (-999). Left alone it drags monthly means toward absurd numbers. POWER values are also gridded estimates for the requested coordinates, so record lat/lon, units and the time standard with every chart.

parameters.name: city
parameters.label: City
parameters.help: Sample mode includes Bengaluru and Chennai only.

parameters.name: compare_city
parameters.label: Compare with
parameters.help: Same method and date range for a second location.

challenges.title: Bengaluru vs. Chennai
challenges.description: Run real mode with compare_city=chennai for the same date range.
challenges.outcome: A comparison chart and one paragraph on the two monsoon regimes.

challenges.title: Beat the baselines
challenges.description: Predict tomorrow's T2M with a linear model on recent days + day-of-year terms.
challenges.outcome: Holdout MAE lower than both persistence and climatology.

challenges.title: Warming trend
challenges.description: Fetch 1985-2024 and fit a trend line to annual mean T2M.
challenges.outcome: Trend in °C/decade with an honest caveat about gridded data.
